name: Vilhon Reach Milk Run
description: A scheduled ground freight service linking merchant markets along the Vilhon and western trade roads.

name: Sword Coast Coasters
description: A scheduled coastal shipping service carrying consolidated cargo between Sword Coast and southern ports.

name: Chult-Tashalar Coastal Freight
description: A southern coastal freight service specializing in perishable and high-value cargo between Chult and Tashalar.

name: Tashalar-Calimshan Freight Line
description: A long-haul coastal carrier linking Calimport, Urbreth and Suldolphor with secure consignments.

name: Waterdeep-Daggerford Caravan Company
description: A Waterdeep caravan house running scheduled wagons south along the Trade Way to Daggerford and the Coast Way markets.

name: North Coast High Road Freight
description: A northern Waterdeep carrier dispatching guarded freight wagons along the High Road to Neverwinter and Luskan.

name: Sword Coast Overland Exchange
description: A Waterdeep forwarding house accepting through consignments along the Sword Coast's long overland routes.

name: The Halls of Hilmer, Master Armorer
description: A Castle Ward armory specializing in fitted plate armor, replacement pieces, and custom commissions.

name: Hriiat Fine Pastries
description: A North Ward bakery selling sweets, meat and fish bite-pies, and filled rolls for travelers on foot.

name: The House of Good Spirits
description: A Southern Ward guild complex with a brewery, wine and spirits production, a forty-bed inn, stables, and meeting rooms.

name: Phalantar's Philtres & Components
description: A Castle Ward apothecary and component dealer financing adventurers and buying unusual finds.

name: Serpentil Books & Folios
description: A Dock Ward bookseller dealing in rare lore, maps, charts, and magical texts.

name: Halambar Lutes & Harps
description: A Castle Ward instrument shop selling new and secondhand stringed instruments and enchanted musical boxes.

name: Balthorr's Rare and Wondrous Treasures
description: A Castle Ward dealer in curios, gems, coins, and regalia with expertise in currencies and insignia.

name: The Old Xoblob Shop
description: A Dock Ward curiosity shop buying adventuring finds, selling unusual gear, and maintaining guarded upper storage.

name: The Old Monster Shop
description: A Southern Ward dealer in live creatures and preserved remains with guarded storage for crated goods.

name: Pelauvir's Counter
description: A Southern Ward general merchandise counter operating from a former warehouse; it does not sell food or drink.

name: Gelfuril the Trader
description: A Dock Ward trader dealing in used goods by barter or coin; explicitly not a pawnshop.

name: Orsabbas's Fine Imports
description: A Trades Ward importer selling far-traveled goods and regional clothing, with seasonal special orders.

name: Helmstar Warehouse
description: A Dock Ward forwarding warehouse handling small cargo with careful packing and discreet service.

name: Red Sails Warehouse
description: A Dock Ward storage house renting longbox space, including premium ice-cooled storage.

name: The Jade Jug
description: Luxury lodging with personal servants, baths and guest transport. Rooms cost 12-30 gp per night and suites cost 25-50 gp.

name: Deepwater Scribes' Exchange
description: A guild-backed bookseller and binder with counters in western centers of learning.

name: Zulkirate Export House
description: A licensed Thayan factor selling regulated magical goods through eastern depots.

name: Golden Sheaf Provisions
description: A temple-chartered milling and baking concern supplying northern roads and cities.

name: Ironstar Forge Company
description: A northern forge company known for consistent steel and warranted weapons.

name: Trade Way Cartwrights
description: A network of cart yards positioned along the busiest caravan exchanges.

name: Amphail Remount Company
description: Breeders, trainers and remount agents serving nobles, guards and caravan masters.

name: Selgaunt Fine Goods Consortium
description: A consortium of factors representing Sembian clothiers and luxury workshops.

name: Cimbar Stone and Scroll
description: A Chessentan partnership combining scholarly imports with builders' materials.

name: Greenscale Reach Packets
description: Hlondeth shipping house running scheduled packet caravels across the Vilhon Reach on the Hlondeth to Arrabar Sea Lane, carrying mixed consignments, passengers and post. Invented for the economy engine; not canon.

name: Arrabar Watermen's Lighterage
description: Lighter and coaster company chartered under Arrabar's Fishers' and Watermen's Guild. Unloads seagoing hulls in Arrabar harbor and runs bulk cargo such as timber and barrels across the Reach to Hlondeth in coasting cogs. Invented for the economy engine; not canon.

name: Red Cask Hulls
description: Merchant-carrier that buys Chondathan common wine at Arrabar and ships it in its own coasting cog to Hlondeth, selling from a dockside cellar there. Carries its own cargo only and is not offered to other shippers. Invented for the economy engine; not canon.

name: The Stag-Horned Flagon
description: Tavern on Amphail's town square, the Malanderways, brewing its own dark barley beer (slaker) and a spicy purple mushroom wine. Run by Krivvin Shamblestar circa 1370 DR and by Arleosa Starhenge circa 1490 DR (Storm King's Thunder, p. 72, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Mushroom wine has no commodity yet; ale stands in for slaker.

name: Goldengulp Brewery
description: Brewery in a two-storey estate near the centre of Goldenfields, close to the longhouses, brewing its namesake beer, Goldengulp, which Northfurrow's End serves. About 60 people worked there in the late 15th century DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 45, 47 and 48, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Ale stands in for Goldengulp; the 60 workers are recorded as lore, not added as engine staff.

name: Mhandyvver's Poultry
specialties: poultry roasted or preserved in oil
description: Barn-like poultry shop on the Long Road in Red Larch, next to Luruth's Tannery and across from Vallivoe's Sundries, selling fowl, fresh eggs and chicks. Run by Oskler Mhandyvver around 1366 DR (Volo's Guide to the North, p. 80) and by his descendant Minthra Mhandyvver and her three children in 1491 DR, when it sold poultry roasted or preserved in oil and eggs fresh or pickled (Princes of the Apocalypse, p. 27, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Chickens stand in for turkeys and ducks; fresh meat stands in for prepared fowl.

name: Chansyrl Fine Harness
description: Harness-maker's workshop in Red Larch founded by Alaglath Chansyrl, who in the 14th century DR also made harness for the wagons built at Thelorn's Safe Journeys (Volo's Guide to the North, p. 80), and run by her granddaughter Phaendra Chansyrl in 1491 DR (Princes of the Apocalypse, pp. 22 to 29, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Thelorn's Safe Journeys
description: Wagonworks in Red Larch owned by the former mercenary Thelorn. In the 14th century DR it kept at least a dozen high-quality wagons in a shed at about 150 gp each and took custom orders needing a tenday each (Volo's Guide to the North, pp. 80 to 81). Described as a busy wagon shop in 1491 DR, when Waelvur's Wagonworks was its rival (Princes of the Apocalypse, pp. 22 to 29, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Luruth's Tannery
description: Tannery on the Long Road in Red Larch, next to Mhandyvver's Poultry, run by the tanner Ulhro Luruth in 1491 DR (Princes of the Apocalypse, pp. 21, 28 to 29, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). The wiki has no article for the tannery itself.

name: Daggerthrust Ales
description: Brewery in Daggerford's River Quarter run by the married couple Halla and Sturgin Brewer, brewing ales and beers in the style of Calimshan's Golden Sands brews and releasing new recipes often. Operating in the late 15th century DR (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, p. 18, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Miller's Dry Goods
description: Dry-goods shop in Daggerford's Caravan Quarter owned by Bess Miller, who also owned three nearby grain mills; sold grain, ground flour and household items. Operating in the late 15th century DR (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, p. 19, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Gublin's Cloth & Cordage
description: Cloth and rope shop in Daggerford's Farmers' Quarter run by Gilly Gublin, with rope-winding machinery from Baldur's Gate's High House of Wonders on its top floor; sold high-quality cloth and cordage, much of it imported, at low prices. Operating in the late 15th century DR (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, p. 19, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Linen stands in for the unspecified cloth.

name: Derval's Smithy
description: Daggerford's leading smithy in the River Quarter, founded by the dwarf Derval Ironeater and run by his grandson Ignal Ironeater; forges weapons in Derval's style for private sale but mainly spear and arrow heads and other metalwork for the town militia. Operating in the late 15th century DR (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, p. 18, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Cromach's Smithy
description: Forge on Daggerford's High Road in the Farmers' Quarter, founded by the human smith Cromach over a century earlier and run by the dwarf Tholvar Cragjaw in the late 15th century DR; makes metal tools, horseshoes and wooden wheels (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, p. 19, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). No wheel commodity exists.

name: Sullerton Shipbuilders
description: Sullerton family shipyard in a large warehouse by Daggerford's River Gate, owned by Wilma Sullerton, building only vessels for the Delimbiyr River; short of lumber when the local logging trade ran into trouble. Operating in the late 15th century DR (Scourge of the Sword Coast, 2014, pp. 9 and 19, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Wainwright's Wagons
description: Long-standing wagon shop in Triboar. In the 14th century DR Skulner Wainwright built the finest wagons in the Dessarin Valley, from about 175 gp (Volo's Guide to the North, pp. 86 to 87); managed by Tosker Wainwright after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 55, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Othovir's Harness Shop
description: Harness shop in Triboar where the craftsman Othovir makes and sells elaborately engraved harness of elk skin; operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, p. 56, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Harness is made only by the tag_harness industry, so the shop sells imported harness (R15).

name: Foehammer's Forge
description: Smithy of the shield dwarf Ghelryn Foehammer in Triboar, whose metalwork was sold in shops across the North and along the Sword Coast (Volo's Guide to the North, p. 86; The North, p. 37); operating after 1485 DR, when Ghelryn was also Royal Armorer of Citadel Felbarr (Storm King's Thunder, p. 57, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Uldinath's Arms
description: Smithy in Triboar founded by the swordsmith Aldenar Uldinath, whose eyebolts, latches, nails and pins supported Wainwright's Wagons in the 14th century DR (Volo's Guide to the North, p. 86); run by Harriet Uldinath after 1485 DR in a friendly rivalry with Foehammer's Forge (Storm King's Thunder, p. 57, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Happy Horse Ranch
description: Ranch and stables west of Triboar where the Karnveller family (Janele, with Aldo, Hingo and Rasko) bred, reared and housed horses for sale; operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 55, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Merivold Pony Park
description: Pony farm at Triboar where the Merivold sisters bred, reared and trained ponies sold as steeds for halflings; operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 55, 57, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: The Cart and Coin
description: Caravan outfitter in Triboar selling caravan gear, supplies and animal feed, selling and exchanging horses and draft animals, and hiring out caravan guards; recorded in the 14th century DR (Volo's Guide to the North, p. 86; The North, p. 37) and owned by Arn and Syreen Widdens after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54, 56, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: The Lion's Share
description: Triboar branch of the Lionshield Coster of Yartar, trading general goods to caravans; operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Offers are inferred from its caravan trade, not listed in the source.

name: Triboar Apothecary
description: Apothecary run by Tarmock Felaskur, operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: The Talking Troll
description: Bar on the Triboar road trade, operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Lodging and food service are not modeled.

name: The Triboar Arms
description: Tavern burned twice and rebuilt, operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Food service is inferred.

name: The Pleasing Platter
description: Restaurant operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Menu is inferred.

name: Everwyvern House
description: Luxury inn for Waterdhavian nobles, operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Lodging is not modeled; offers are the table.

name: Northshield House
description: Inn operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Lodging is not modeled; offers are the table.

name: Six Windows
description: Boarding house operating after 1485 DR (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Lodging is not modeled; offers are the table.

name: The Triboar Travelers (Waterdeep Run)
description: Caravan company renting wagons to merchants for trips to Waterdeep along the Long Road, with set return-trip prices (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Fleet sizes are an estimate.

name: The Triboar Travelers (Everlund Run)
description: Caravan company renting wagons to merchants for trips to Everlund by the Evermoor Way, with set return-trip prices (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 54 to 58, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Fleet sizes are an estimate.

name: Barthen's Provisions
description: Phandalin's largest trading post, run by Elmar Barthen with clerks Ander and Thistle and open from dawn to dusk in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 14 to 16). Sold adventuring gear, rations and simple goods but no weapons, armour or potions; loaded and unloaded the wagons in and out of town, brokered livestock sales, supplied Tibor Wester's logging camp and carried Butterskull Ranch's skull-shaped butter in the early 1490s DR (Dragon of Icespire Peak, pp. 8 to 9, 34). Closed in late 1495 or early 1496 DR (Acquisitions Incorporated, pp. 108 to 109). All via the Forgotten Realms Wiki; offers are inferred from that description.

name: Lionshield Coster (Phandalin post)
description: Phandalin trading post of the Lionshield Coster of Yartar, selling weapons and armour shipped in from the coster; run by Linene Graywind in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 16 to 17) and with her daughter Minghee by 1496 DR (Acquisitions Incorporated, p. 105), via the Forgotten Realms Wiki. Specific weapon types are inferred.

name: Phandalin Miner's Exchange
description: Trading post and guildhall that weighs and buys ore and gems from local miners, registers claims and sells goods; the best place in Phandalin to buy carts and wagons. Run by the Zhentarim agent Halia Thornton in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 16 to 17) and by Sharna Quirstiron by 1496 DR; it often went months without revenue in the early 1490s DR (Acquisitions Incorporated, pp. 105 to 108). Via the Forgotten Realms Wiki. Ore and gem purchasing is not modeled.

name: Edermath Orchard
description: Apple orchard and cider mill on the north-west side of Phandalin kept by Daran Edermath, a retired marshal, in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 15 to 16); fresh fruit and juice in summer, cider in winter, sold to visiting merchants and local inns; employing out-of-work miners by 1496 DR (Acquisitions Incorporated, pp. 101, 107). Via the Forgotten Realms Wiki. Cider has no commodity; fruit stands in for apples.

name: Stonehill Inn
description: Two-storey inn near the centre of Phandalin with six guest rooms, run by Toblen and Trilena Stonehill, who came from Triboar; a bed cost 5 sp a night and a meal about 1 sp, with ale and cider served, in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 14 to 15, 18; Dragon of Icespire Peak, p. 8), via the Forgotten Realms Wiki. Lodging is not modeled; the menu is inferred.

name: The Sleeping Giant
description: Rundown tap house at the east end of Phandalin's main street run by the dwarf Grista Kettlecopp, frequented by miners and by the Redbrands in 1491 DR (Lost Mine of Phandelver, p. 18) and still open, more worn, in 1496 DR (Acquisitions Incorporated, p. 108), via the Forgotten Realms Wiki.

name: Lionshield Coster
description: Merchant company based in Yartar (lion's head on a shield, often on blue) operating across the greater Dessarin Valley in the 15th century DR, shipping finished goods such as armour and weapons to small settlements; posts at Phandalin (1491 DR), Nightstone and the Lion's Share in Triboar (Lost Mine of Phandelver, pp. 16 to 17; Storm King's Thunder, pp. 25, 54, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). Offers are inferred from the Phandalin post; the Yartar house's own stock is not described.

name: Singing Sprite
description: Slate-roofed stone inn facing the Seven-Stringed Harp across a muddy crossing of lanes in Secomber, with a never-closing common dining room, meeting rooms the townsfolk hire constantly and a copper bathtub in every room. Built by the human wizard Ganatharas and named for his late sprite wife Lathiril Shrune; owned by the gnome Windfeather family, whose innkeeper on duty is Heverseer Windfeather or one of his three brothers, working in shifts (Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast, 1994, pp. 83 to 85, set 1367 DR; The North, 1996, p. 64). Rooms were 10 to 17 gp a night with hot baths, clothes-mending and stabling, ale 6 cp a tankard, mead, milk and wine 2 gp a tallglass, and platters or stew bowls 7 gp with two drinks. The menu names green Delimbiyr river crabs, roast lamb, venison and beef, fowl stew and cheese-stuffed crackers, with steamed greens bought from local gardens. Operation in 1492 DR is not verified. Lodging is not modeled; offers are inferred from the menu (river crabs stand in as fresh fish) and staff beyond the four brothers is assumed.

secomber.street: Pond crossing, opposite the Seven-Stringed Harp

name: Seven-Stringed Harp
description: Ramshackle, many-winged tavern at the lowest spot in Secomber, beside a horse pond in the bowl between the three hills, with a huge hitching rail, a floating, glowing harp (a permanent spell by the mage Amelior Amanitas) and servants' passages hidden behind tapestries. Locals meet there, merchants do business and hire guards, and three to seven bards play for free most nights; it is where the Ballad of the Dream Weaver was first heard, sung by the half-elven bard Talanthe Truesilver about 40 winters before 1367 DR, when it was called the Stag (Volo's Guide to the Sword Coast, 1994, pp. 80 to 82; The North, 1996, p. 64). Staff are young would-be harpists. Ale was 3 cp a tankard, stout 5 cp, minty white wine 6 cp a tallglass and plates 1 sp (salted biscuits with snails or small fish, or peppered mushrooms rolled in melted cheese). The owner is not named; operation in 1492 DR is not verified. Offers are inferred from the menu (biscuits as bread, small fish as salt fish) and staff counts are assumed.

secomber.street: Pond crossing, beside the horse pond

name: Samril's Fine Blades
description: Halfling workshop in Secomber, run by the Samril family, that finished raw blades from the Arthane Furnace in Beliard by sharpening and polishing them and fitting grips of local duskwood and blueleaf, leather wraps and copper wire, then sent them to the Arthane Armory in Waterdeep. Suppliers named on the same map include the woodcutter Maraszymo Darluth in the High Forest, Gleskur's Finemetals (copper wire), Anastur's Abrasives in Llorkh and Sorkryn's Soft Hides in Scornubel (Ed Greenwood, "Thaelon Morgyr's Map", Forging the Realms, 2013, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). The source is undated; operation in 1492 DR is not verified. The finished blade stands in as `sword`; the raw blades are bought in, so the stock records finishing only, and staff counts are assumed.

name: Gleskur's Finemetals of Secomber
description: Dwarf metal workshop in Secomber supplying braided copper wire for the sword grips finished at Samril's Fine Blades (Ed Greenwood, "Thaelon Morgyr's Map", Forging the Realms, 2013, via the Forgotten Realms Wiki). The source is undated and names no individual; operation in 1492 DR is not verified. Copper wire is not a commodity, so the shop offers none and is recorded as a service; `copper_ingot` would be its input. Staff counts are assumed.
services: braided copper wire for sword grips

name: Waelvur's Wagonworks
description: Ilmeth Waelvur ran a rival wagon workshop in 1491 DR (Princes of the Apocalypse, pp. 24, 27, via Forgotten Realms Wiki). Carts and quantities are not established. Business offers, unit stock, worker allocations, ability scores and address fields are simulation scenarios, not attested canon; this registry identifies existing 1491 DR village activity and does not increase settlement industry output.

description: Albaeri Mellikho operated a stoneworks with stonecutters in 1491 DR (Princes of the Apocalypse, p. 28, via Forgotten Realms Wiki); the kind of stone is not established, so no granite, marble or bricks are offered.
